note: On the bofop family the generalization gap decays with sample size at a log-log slope close to the -1/2 predicted by the covering-number / equicontinuity argument. Removing the fiber bound (heavy-tailed degrees, non-compact DIDM space) degrades either the rate or the absolute gap, showing the bofop hypothesis is doing real work. Empirical corroboration of the mechanism, not a reproduction of the paper's explicit constants (none are numerically stated). CAVEAT: the non-bofop mutation raises the gap LEVEL by 2-11x at every m but does NOT degrade its asymptotic slope in this regime, so the experiment supports the vanishing-error claim and the usefulness of the fiber bound as a constant, without isolating compactness as necessary for the rate itself.
